summary.title: How Does the Internet Work?
summary.one_liner: You learn how data moves across the Internet: TCP/IP protocol stacks, packets, IP addressing, routers, DNS, and how HTTP and SMTP run on top of TCP.
takeaways: Data is split into packets, passed down the TCP/IP stack, routed hop by hop via routers, then reassembled at the destination.
TCP handles reliable, ordered delivery and uses port numbers to choose the receiving application; IP handles addressing and routing without guarantees.
DNS servers translate domain names to IP addresses, and each holds only part of the database.
HTTP is a connectionless text protocol that opens a new connection per request, while SMTP is connection-oriented and command-driven.
IPv4 offers about 2^32 addresses, which motivates IPv6.
summary.summary: This 2002 whitepaper by Rus Shuler gives a basic, non-deep overview of how the Internet functions. It walks through an example of sending a message between two IP addresses, showing how the TCP/IP protocol stack adds ports and addresses, how routers and ISP backbones forward packets, and how DNS resolves names. It then explains HTTP and SMTP as application protocols and describes TCP and IP behaviour, ending with notes on IPv4 limits and a list of references and RFCs.
